title: Will the United States attack Oman before 2027?
resolution_criteria: This question will resolve as **Yes** if, before January 1, 2027, the United States carries out a military attack against Oman's territory or military forces. This can be purposefully or accidentally.
fine_print:
Oman's territory includes territorial waters.

To qualify, the attack will need to target or physically harm Omani buildings, infrastructure, vessels, military forces, or nationals. Cyberattacks, warning shots, and strikes that cause no such harm will not count, regardless of where they land.

If it is disputed whether the United States is responsible for an attack, this question will refer to credible sources or may resolve as **ambiguous**. In case of an attack where there is no credible source consensus that it occurred within Oman's territory and neither the US nor Oman claims that it did, this question will not resolve based on that incident.

comments.author: Vlad25
comments.text: I think that a deliberate US attack is unlikely given their strategic relationship. However, with the ongoing military activity that is going on around the Strait of Hormuz, I believe that there is a small risk of accidental escalation or miscalculation that will result in an attack on Oman.

comments.author: VectorWright
comments.text:
Good catch by sai\_39 and DeRuina on the two explicit Trump threats to bomb Oman this year, May 27 and August 17, which I didn't weight heavily enough before reading this thread. Those aren't nothing. A sitting president naming a specific country as a bombing target twice in one year is unusual even by this administration's standards.



But DeRuina's framing on the fine print is the part that actually matters for calibration: this resolves YES on any US strike that harms Omani vessels, infrastructure, or nationals, deliberate or accidental, and the US has been hitting Iranian boats and tankers in the Gulf of Oman and the Strait since March, some of it inside Omani waters. Six months of that operational tempo have produced zero documented Omani harm from US fire. That's a real empirical base rate for the accidental pathway, not just a hypothetical, and it argues against overweighting the two threats into something higher.



On the deliberate side, the diplomatic counterevidence is stacking up. Rubio called Al Busaidi on September 15, and Reuters reported Oman hosted a US-Houthi meeting at its embassy in Muscat on September 16, both after the August threat. That's Washington actively using Oman as a channel, not squaring up to it.



I'm landing at 7%, above the community's 3% given the two explicit threats and the ongoing military activity in Omani waters, but well below sai\_39's 10% or Russell-viper's 15%, since six months of zero accidental harm and the active diplomatic cooperation since the last threat both cut the other way.

comments.author: DeRuina
comments.text: The May 27 and August 17 threats get most of the attention, but I think the fine print makes deliberate policy almost beside the point. YES resolves on any US strike that harms Omani vessels, infrastructure or nationals, including accidents. That is the channel I would actually watch. The US has been hitting Iranian boats and tankers in the Gulf of Oman and the Strait since March, part of it inside Omani waters, and two US aircraft have gone down off Oman's coast. Six months of that tempo has produced zero documented Omani harm from US fire, which is a real empirical base rate, not a hypothetical. The Rubio call to Al Busaidi on September 15 (The National) also suggests Washington is now courting Muscat, not squaring up to it. What would move me is a struck Omani-flagged dhow or fishing boat with disputed attribution. If a US strike hits a vessel with unconfirmed Omani registration, would the resolver wait for an official Omani government statement before ruling on this question?

comments.author: sai_39
comments.text:
The May threat followed reports that Iran and Oman had discussed jointly administering or charging ships for passage through the strait. Trump’s position was that no country should “control” the waterway. [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/may/28/first-thing-trump-threatens-oman-strait-of-hormuz) reported this context directly. Broadly speaking, US wants Iran to act more like a US-aligned partner instead of a neutral intermediary. Trump’s [August statement](https://www.foxnews.com/world/trump-confirms-irgc-backchannel-calls-irans-white-flag-surrender) came while discussing a new direct backchannel that bypassed traditional mediators.

The threats therefore appear designed to frighten Oman away from policies Washington dislikes. They are unusually explicit, but Trump often uses extreme military threats to strengthen bargaining leverage.

But the strongest evidence against an attack is Washington’s continuing behaviour toward Oman:

* Oman provides strategically useful military access, including ports capable of accommodating US aircraft carriers.
* On September 16, Reuters reported that Oman helped organise a meeting between US officials and Houthi representatives at the US Embassy in Muscat. Strong evidence that operational cooperation continues despite Trump’s rhetoric. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-officials-met-iran-backed-houthis-oman-over-weekend-sources-say-2026-09-16/)
* Trump is expected to meet Oman alongside other GCC states over the Iran war’s future, and has said he hopes the war is approaching its end. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-hold-talks-iran-with-gulf-leaders-next-week-axios-reports-2026-09-16/)

I think the crowd is too low given that the accidental pathway deserves almost as much weight as the deliberate one.

comments.author: sheikah
Theomachado
comments.text:
@(Deranged_saint)

I partially agreed on the frame, but 13% is too high. Threat-to-execution is 0 for 2 with a test in between. Trump threatened Oman on 27 May and 17 August. Nine days after the second, Oman and Iran announced the phased strait framework, exactly the "getting in the way" the threat named. Nothing followed. The rationale was removed on 25 August when the US Navy cleared the Hormuz mines itself. The Oman track is de-escalating even as the Iran track escalates. The embassy returned to routine visa services on 1 September. Markets agree. Oman 5Y CDS is about 77bp versus Saudi at 54bp, below its own March war-start reading of about 89bp. The 17 August threat moved it about 4bp.

On (5) the chain runs backward. Striking Oman adds an oil risk premium rather than crashing prices. A crash needs Hormuz reopened, which an attack through the mediation channel would destroy. Anyway, this is a big game theory model pivoted on Trump in the center, who is a very unpredictable figure, so the 13% may seem high but may be a hedge on that as wel
